item.title: Stiff source terms inside ADER-DG method
item.description: arXiv:2610.30852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ADER-DG numerical method with the LST-DG predictor, when used to solve hyperbolic equations with stiff source terms, exhibits properties characteristic of IMEX computational schemes. With increasing stiffness, characterized by the parameter $z = \nu{\Delta t}^{n} < 0$, the maximum of the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}$ of the ADER-DG numerical method increases. In the region of strong stiffness $|z| \gg 1$, a linear increase in the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z) \sim |z|$ occurs. In the region of small source terms $|z| \ll 1$, the results $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z)$ transform into known results for the problem $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(0)$ without source terms. In the transition region $|z| \sim 1$, a range of insignificant decrease in the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z)$ is discovered. In the linear case, instability is violated precisely when one of the matrix eigenvalues reaches $\lambda = -1$, regardless of the phase $\theta$ of the numerical solution. A rigorous stability theory of the ADER-DG numerical method for stiff problems for arbitrary degree $N$ of basis polynomials is constructed. The stability condition is simplified to solving a polynomial equation for the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}$. Highly accurate dependencies of the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(N, z)$ of the ADER-DG method on the parameter $z$ are obtained. A rigorous direct proof of the approximation of the ADER-DG method is presented. Approximation orders $p = N+1$ for arbitrary degrees $N$ are rigorously derived. A set of numerical experiments is carried out to apply the ADER-DG method to solving both a linear advection-reaction equation and the system of Euler equations for a two-component reacting medium. The results obtained in these calculations confirm the theoretical results well.
item.dc:creator: I. S. Popov, A. P. Popova

item.title: Extended-regularized lattice Boltzmann method
item.description: arXiv:2610.31072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regularized lattice Boltzmann methods improve numerical stability by projecting the nonequilibrium distribution onto its hydrodynamic second-order Hermite sector and filtering the remaining kinetic modes. We introduce a separate relaxation time for the complete complementary kinetic subspace. The resulting extended-regularized lattice Boltzmann method (E-RLBM) interpolates continuously between the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook and regularized collision operators while retaining a two-rate implementation. A Chapman-Enskog expansion shows that the isothermal Navier-Stokes equations are recovered with kinematic viscosity $\nu=c_s^2(\tau-\Delta t/2)$, independently of the kinetic relaxation time $\tau_{\rm nh}$, whereas $\tau_{\rm nh}$ changes higher-order truncation errors. For linear transverse shear, its first effect is a fourth-derivative term whose coefficient depends on the direction of propagation relative to the lattice. This fourth-order coefficient is affine in $\tau_{\rm nh}$. For linear shear on D2Q9 and $\tau_{\rm nh}$ between $\tau$ and $\Delta t$, it lies between the corresponding BGK and RLBM values in every propagation direction. Stability maps for the decaying Taylor-Green vortex and flow past a rectangular obstacle show that an appropriate kinetic relaxation substantially enlarges the stable parameter domain. In a Taylor-Green convergence test with consistent initialization, all three operators converge at second order, and their error differences follow the hyperviscous coefficient for diagonal shear waves: the E-RLBM error is about 6% above the BGK error and about 40% below the RLBM error; in a double shear layer at Re = 80000, the E-RLBM follows the RLBM convergence curve. The proposed collision operator therefore provides a low-cost means of controlling nonhydrodynamic modes without introducing a full multiple-relaxation-time basis.
item.dc:creator: Lu\'is Orlando Emerich dos Santos, Diogo Nardelli Siebert

item.title: Influence of nanoparticle shapes in nanofluid film boiling on vertical cylinders: A numerical study
item.description: arXiv:2610.31151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This research explores how nanoparticle shapes affect the thermal behavior of nanofluid film boiling along a vertical cylinder, using a Continuous-Species-Transfer method within a Computational Multi-Fluid Dynamics framework. The behavior of nanoparticles in both liquid and vapor phases is modeled, accounting for Brownian motion and thermophoresis. A comprehensive two-dimensional axisymmetric analysis is conducted to investigate the effects of various Al2O3 nanoparticle shapes, including spheres, bricks, blades, cylinders, and platelets, on boiling heat transfer. The results demonstrate that nanoparticle shape has a minimal impact on deposition dynamics but significantly affects kinematic viscosity, particularly for platelet-shaped nanoparticles. Blade-shaped nanoparticles provide substantial enhancement of thermal transport, as indicated by pronounced temperature gradients and increased thermal conductivity. These nanoparticles also improve the Nusselt number, suggesting enhanced boiling heat transfer efficiency. This improvement is particularly significant at higher nanoparticle concentrations, although the relationship is not strictly linear. Future work will explore different nanoparticle materials, boiling scenarios, and experimental validation.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Yahyaee, A. "Influence of nanoparticle shapes in nanofluid film boiling on vertical cylinders: A numerical study." International Journal of Thermofluids 22 (2024): 100631
item.dc:creator: Ali Yahyaee

item.title: Bridge change-of-measure for propagator estimation of diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The propagator of one-dimensional diffusions has relevant applications in statistical inference and across many disciplines. Yet it is obtained in closed form only for very few simple models. Here we analyze an importance sampling strategy based on a bridge change of measure to estimate propagators: paths are generated under an auxiliary diffusion whose bridge between the two fixed boundary points is easy to generate, and the target propagator is recovered through a Radon-Nikodym derivative or likelihood ratio correction derived from Girsanov's theorem. This method overcomes the main limitations of the crude Monte Carlo estimator, which relies on binning in state space, introducing bias and becoming inefficient with rare transitions. We apply the method to a range of benchmark processes and show that the bridge-based estimator matches the accuracy of crude Monte Carlo with orders of magnitude fewer sample paths. Finally, we elaborate on discretization schemes for the Radon-Nikodym derivative and on approximations to the best-in-class change of measure, both of which increase the efficiency of the method.
item.dc:creator: Javier Aguilar, Riccardo Gatto

item.title: QuDPy-FDGF: A Python-Based Tool for Computing Ultrafast Nonlinear Optical Responses Using Frequency Domain Green's Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present QuDPy-FDGF, an open-source Python framework that evaluates Liouville-space pathways as hybrid chains of time propagators and frequency-domain Green's functions. Frequency-resolved intervals are computed directly through shifted linear systems, without time propagation followed by a Fourier transform, while other intervals may remain in the time domain. A model-agnostic block interface separates the physical model from pathway construction, numerical propagation, and detection. The released implementation provides an explicit dense Liouville-space backend for reference calculations and a sector-resolved sparse backend using matrix-free generator actions, Krylov time propagation, and generalized minimal residual (GMRES) resolvent solves. Its observable layer reuses propagated pathway responses to evaluate operator expectation values, action-detected readout interactions, instantaneous jump rates, and integrated mean jump counts. The framework is assessed on an analytically solvable open two-level system and on two examples of increasing complexity: the complete third-order rephasing response, with its eight sequences, of a thermally initialized anisotropic Heisenberg (XXZ) spin chain with unequal excitation sectors, and two coupled dissipative anharmonic modes whose spectra depend on the detected observable, with the fifth-order double-quantum response of their closed limit. The calculations reproduce the analytical two-level response, check the matrix-free sparse evaluation against the dense assembly of the generator, and recover the harmonic-limit cancellation of the fifth-order signal when the required three-excitation manifold is retained. QuDPy-FDGF therefore provides a unified framework for pathway- and observable-resolved nonlinear spectroscopy in finite or truncated Hilbert spaces with unitary or Markovian Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Desmarais, Sim\'on Paiva-Ortega, F\'elix Brunell, Eric R. Bittner, Hao Li, Carlos Silva-Acu\~na

item.title: Multigroup Radiation Diffusion with Compton Scattering on a Moving Mesh: Implementation in RICH and Application to Tidal Disruption Events
item.description: arXiv:2610.31324v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Compton scattering exchanges energy between radiation and hot gas and changes the spectrum in high-energy astrophysical systems such as tidal disruption events (TDEs). Because it couples all photon energies and can act faster than the hydrodynamic time step, many radiation-hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations omit its spectral redistribution or treat its energy exchange in the gray approximation. We extend the multigroup flux-limited diffusion module of the moving-mesh RHD code RICH to include Compton scattering with the exact thermal Compton kernel. In our semi-implicit scheme for the thermal radiative transfer equation, the temperature dependence of the kernel enters a generalized Fleck factor, and the group Compton operator conserves photon number and satisfies detailed balance. In equilibration tests, the scheme agrees with independent solutions, relaxes without absorption and emission to a Bose-Einstein spectrum, and remains stable for time steps that do not resolve the Compton equilibration timescale. We apply it to a three-dimensional simulation of the disruption of a $0.5\,M_\odot$ star by a $10^6\,M_\odot$ black hole. We find that during the X-ray flash, inverse Compton scattering dominates the coupling between the gas and the radiation near the nozzle shock, where it adds X-ray energy much faster than thermal emission and may affect the dynamics. Outside the X-ray thermalization radii, its instantaneous X-ray production rate during the flash is comparable to or larger than the escaping X-ray luminosity, so it may contribute substantially to the X-ray emission from TDEs.
item.dc:creator: Itamar Giron, Menahem Krief, Elad Steinberg

item.title: Energy-dependent trapping of backscattered helium during magnetron sputtering growth: A molecular dynamics study
item.description: arXiv:2610.13509v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Helium incorporation during magnetron sputtering can strongly affect thin film growth and lead to the formation of gas/solid nanocomposites and nanoporous structures. Here, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are used to investigate the trapping mechanism of helium atoms (He) and the subsequent formation of He bubbles during the sputter deposition of aluminum (Al) and titanium (Ti) thin films. The simulations account for the kinetic energy distributions of sputtered metal atoms and backscattered gas species. Results indicate that He is efficiently incorporated into the growing films, leading to the formation of high-pressure, dense He bubbles, with a much higher He-to-metal atomic ratio in Ti ($\sim$ 60%) than in Al ($\sim$ 12%). More importantly, the simulations reveal a clear energy dependence of He trapping in Ti: background He atoms at thermal energies are essentially not incorporated, whereas efficient trapping starts at an incident energy of approximately 20 eV and increases up to a saturation regime near 100 eV. Simulated thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) further reveals distinct release mechanisms in the two investigated metals: He desorption from Al occurs at higher temperatures and is preceded by the removal of surface Al atoms, whereas He and Ti atom desorption starts continuously around 950 K, leading to a porous structure. Comparative simulations with argon (Ar) demonstrate negligible trapping even at comparable kinetic energy or momentum, showing that neither parameter alone accounts for the strong He incorporation observed in Ti. The above results are in very good agreement with what is reported in literature for low-kinetic energy He ion implantation in metal surfaces, suggesting similar insertion mechanisms. They clarify the atomistic conditions governing noble gas trapping during film growth and provide a basis for controlling He incorporation and porosity in films synthesized by magnetron sputtering.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Brault (GREMI, MS4ALL), Anne-Lise Thomann (GREMI), Alejandro Borroto (GREMI)

item.title: Self-Adaptive Model-Order Reduction for Shock-Dominated Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.15944v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Projection-based model-order reduction (MOR) offers a promising approach for accelerating expensive full-order model (FOM) by constructing reduced-order models (ROMs) that retain the majority of FOM accuracy while significantly reducing the computational cost. However, conventional static ROMs, often following offline/online training strategy, can exhibit limited predictive capability for convection-dominated problems featuring strongly evolving physics such as shocks. Adaptive ROMs emerge as a promising alternative and address such limitation by dynamically updating the low-dimensional subspace during online simulation to track locally evolving system dynamics, thereby enabling accurate predictions even for shock-dominated flows. However, such online adaptation introduces additional computational overhead, and frequent basis and sampling-point updates can substantially reduce their computational advantage relative to their static counterpart. To reconcile this tradeoff, the current work introduces a self-adaptive MOR framework that dynamically constructs and deploys the most appropriate ROM formulation (either adaptive or static) on the fly according to the evolving characteristics of the solution. to achieve optimal computational efficiency while maintaining high modeling accuracy of the local physics during the online model execution. In this regard, the proposed framework seeks to exploit the advantages of both adaptive- and static-ROM approaches to achieve an optimal computational efficiency and predictive accuracy while reducing reliance on extensive offline training. The framework is developed and evaluated for modeling rotating detonation engines (RDEs), which provide a challenging test environment involving strongly convection-dominated, transient, and multiscale reacting-flow dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Ali Mohaghegh, Cheng Huang

item.title: An Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator for coupled surrogate morphodynamic modelling
item.description: arXiv:2610.22432v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Morphodynamic simulations require repeated coupling between hydrodynamic solvers, sediment transport modules, and bed updating. For long duration, multi-scenario simulations on large unstructured meshes, such coupling is computationally demanding. This study proposes an Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator (AH-GNO) that formulates bed evolution as a graph operator learning problem from recent hydrodynamic and topographic states to predict future bed elevation increments. The model operates directly on the native unstructured meshes. The approach integrates area-weighted graph learning, historical state selection, and forecast horizon estimation, allowing the effective history length (K) and update interval (B) to vary with the evolving flow and bed state. Using Telemac2D/GAIA solutions as supervised numerical references, the framework is evaluated on the official Bump and Yen bend benchmarks and on a field-scale application (Waiho River, New Zealand). Results show that the AH-GNO reproduces the main patterns of bedform migration, bend-scale erosion and deposition, and localized bed adjustment. Across the three cases, the tested CPU-GPU deployment reduced post-training bed-update workflow time from 12~1204 s with GAIA to 0.08~3.34 s with AH-GNO. This improvement corresponds to deployment-specific accelerations of approximately 150~360 times relative to 4-core GAIA CPU configurations, and with 105~186 times gains for 20-core CPU configurations. These results suggest that, while retaining hydrodynamic feedback from TELEMAC-2D, a learned operator for bed updating can provide an efficient acceleration component for morphodynamic scenario analysis and rapid coupled simulation.
item.dc:creator: Ying Cao, Yifan Yang, Junqiang Xia, Julia C. Mullarney, M\'ario J. Franca

item.title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.29909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Machine-learning surrogates in computational science often require not only accurate predictions but also expectations, variances, conserved integrals, and normalization constants. Conventional neural networks, including Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs), generally evaluate these quantities through Monte Carlo sampling or multidimensional quadrature, making repeated inference costly, particularly in high dimensions. We introduce KANs with Tractable Operators for Uncertainty and Constraints (TOUCKANs), whose finite-degree polynomial outer functions yield a decomposable sum--product representation. Under factorizing input measures, expectations and higher moments then reduce algebraically to deterministic recursions over one-dimensional leaf integrals. Independent and shared inner-block variants form a parameter-efficiency hierarchy, and a universal-approximation proof for its most restricted member extends to the complete class. The same deterministic operators allow conserved integrals and normalization to be imposed throughout training. Across uniform and Gaussian benchmarks through 50 dimensions, deterministic mean and variance errors remained below the median fixed-budget Monte Carlo errors in every case. TOUCKANs also conserved Cahn--Hilliard mass to machine precision and imposed normalization and orthogonality through deterministic moments, enabling joint computation of the lowest four Schr\"odinger eigenpairs in two, three, and five dimensions. TOUCKANs therefore connect KAN approximation with tractable probabilistic circuits, making statistical operators and integral constraints directly available within an expressive neural surrogate.
item.dc:creator: Juan Diego Toscano, Sascha Ranftl, Zhiwei Gao, Li-Lian Wang, George Em Karniadakis

item.title: CENIC: Convex Error-controlled Numerical Integration for Contact
item.description: arXiv:2511.08771v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: State-of-the-art robotics simulators operate in discrete time. This requires users to choose a time step, which is both critical and challenging: large steps can produce non-physical artifacts, while small steps force the simulation to run slowly. Continuous-time error-controlled integration avoids such issues by automatically adjusting the time step to achieve a desired accuracy. But existing error-controlled integrators struggle with the stiff dynamics of contact, and cannot meet the speed and scalability requirements of modern robotics workflows. We introduce CENIC, a new variable-step integrator that brings together recent advances in convex time-stepping and error-controlled integration, inheriting benefits from both continuous integration and discrete time-stepping. CENIC runs at fast real-time rates comparable to discrete-time robotics simulators like MuJoCo, Drake and Isaac Sim, while also providing guarantees on accuracy and convergence.
item.dc:creator: Vince Kurtz, Alejandro Castro

item.title: A coupled finite element formulation for chemo-mechano-thermodynamical contact and its application to bonding and debonding
item.description: arXiv:2606.12375v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work presents a finite element formulation for coupled chemo-mechano-thermodynamical large deformation contact. The formulation is based on the contact theory of Sauer et al. (2022) that contains six coupled (but separate) fields: the deformation and temperature of the two contacting bodies, as well as an interfacial bonding field and interfacial temperature. The latter is governed by the chemical and mechanical energy dissipation at the interface. Here the focus is placed on the evolution of bonding and debonding, and how it is coupled to the mechanical and thermal contact state. Several elementary models are proposed for this based on a quadratic contact potential. The resulting contact formulation becomes very general and versatile, which is illustrated by several challenging examples. They include pressure- and gap- dependent bonding, exothermic bonding reactions, thermal hardening and thermal expansion, as well as simultaneous bonding and debonding. They are based on a monolithic finite element implementation using classical and isogeometric shape functions together with implicit time integration. Its full linearization, required for the Newton-Raphson solution method, is also provided for the six-field problem, as well as for several of its simplifications. If bonding sites are material points, the bonding variable can be condensed-out locally.
item.dc:creator: Roger A. Sauer

item.title: PDECheck: A Diagnostic Software Suite for Auditing Learned PDE Simulators
item.description: arXiv:2606.18200v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: PDECheck audits learned PDE simulators through callable propagators or saved predictions. It evaluates relative $L^2$ error, temporal composition, finite-difference generators, and equation-specific physical residuals, retaining horizons and missing prerequisites. Analytic and manufactured defects verify the kernels. A heat-equation sweep quantifies generator sensitivity to timestep, frequency, grid, and precision. A three-equation, five-seed FNO study compares supervised, PINO-style, and composition-regularized training. An accuracy-matched advection comparison has state errors below 0.3% and a semigroup-error ratio of 1.48 (95% interval 1.34-1.62). The composition penalty lowers semigroup error but increases composed-state and longer-rollout prediction error. A time-reparameterization check produces identical low-error endpoints with different compositions. Applications to five external equation families exercise the readers and physical contracts on coarse grids. The release includes reproducibility artifacts and measured CPU/CUDA costs.
item.dc:creator: Lennon J. Shikhman
